judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The 'Job Vacancies' service card is an <a href="/careers"> that wraps an <article> holding an SVG and a span with the text. In the snapshot's CDP tree, Chrome gives the link the name "". Chromium does not compute name from content through an article, so the span text never reaches the link. I looked for a reason it might pass. Rampa's own name and axe-style computation (accname step 2F/2H) both give 'Job Vacancies', so Firefox and screen-reader browse mode may still read the text. Even so, the platform accessibility API in Chrome and Edge, which most screen-reader users run, exposes no name, and voice control and link lists depend on that name. So the name cannot be programmatically determined there. The live HTML has the same markup. The part of the message saying a screen reader 'announces only link' overstates things, but the core claim names the real failure.
